## 14.1 Record a sample in Audacity

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Set the project rate to 48000 Hz and record one channel (mono).
- Watch the meter first, so that the peaks stay near −6 dB.
- Record 2 seconds of room tone, then three takes of the sound.
- **Do it:** Record three takes of a short sound. Which settings did you use?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/edit-steps.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 1 · Settings

a) Which project rate do you set for a game sound?
b) How many recording channels does one sound source need?
c) What do you record before the three takes?

::: {.answer}
a) 48000 Hz
b) one channel (mono)
c) 2 seconds of room tone
:::

## 14.2 Trim, noise reduction and fades

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Trim deletes the silence before and after the best take.
- Noise Reduction learns the hum from the room tone and removes it.
- A short fade-out at the end removes the click.
- **Do it:** Clean your best take. Which step changed the sound most?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/before-after.png)
:::
::::

## Example · Cleaning the meow

The best meow starts 0.9 s late, has a fridge hum and ends with a click.
**Which three edits does Yara make, in which order?**

::: {.reveal}
1. **Trim:** she deletes the silence and leaves 0.05 s.
2. **Noise Reduction:** she takes the profile from the room tone and applies it to the take.
3. **Fade Out:** the last 0.2 s fades to silence, so the click is gone.
:::

## Try it 2 · Cleaning

a) The meow starts almost a second late. Which edit fixes it?
b) A low hum runs under the whole take. Which tool removes it?
c) Where does Noise Reduction get its noise profile?

::: {.answer}
a) trim the silence at the start
b) Noise Reduction
c) from the room tone
:::

## 14.3 Normalize and export

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Normalize raises the loudest peak of the clean take to −1 dB.
- A sound effect is exported as a WAV with 16 bits in mono.
- The name says the type, what and the version, with no spaces.
- **Do it:** Export your sample as a WAV. Which name did you give it?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/export-names.png)
:::
::::

## Example · The meow is ready

The cleaned meow lasts about 1 second, and its loudest peak is at −14 dB.
**How does Yara make it ready for the game?**

::: {.reveal}
1. She **normalizes** the take to −1 dB, with no clipping.
2. She exports a WAV with 16 bits in mono, about **94 KB**.
3. She names it **sfx_pasha_meow_01.wav** and adds it to the sound list.
:::

## Try it 3 · Ready for the game

a) To which level do you normalize a sound effect?
b) Why do you normalize after the cleaning?
c) Which name fits the meow?

::: {.answer}
a) −1 dB
b) Otherwise the noise and the clicks get louder too.
c) sfx_pasha_meow_01.wav
:::

## Try it 4 · Order and size (harder)

a) Why can no edit repair a clipped take?
b) How big is 2 seconds of a 48 kHz, 16-bit mono WAV?
c) Which name fits the second version of a splash sound?

::: {.answer}
a) The flat tops of the wave are lost.
b) about 188 KB
c) sfx_splash_02.wav
:::

## Summary

- We record at 48000 Hz in mono, with the peaks near −6 dB.
- We clean in order: trim, Noise Reduction and fades.
- We normalize to −1 dB after the cleaning and never amplify into clipping.
- We export a WAV with a name like sfx_what_01.wav.
